Sure, here's an example of a curl command to call an API server:


```bash
curl -X GET https://api.example.com/users/1234 -H 'Authorization: Bearer your\_token\_here'
```
In this example, we are making a GET request to the API endpoint at `https://api.example.com/users/1234`, where `1234` is the ID of the user we want to retrieve. We are also including an `Authorization` header with a bearer token.

Note that you'll need to replace `https://api.example.com` with the actual URL of the API server you want to call, and replace `your_token_here` with an actual authentication token that you've obtained through the proper channels.

Also, keep in mind that the specific syntax of the curl command may vary depending on the API server you're working with and the type of request you're making (e.g. GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.). Please tell me how to add parameters to curl command
Answer in English.
rounds.assistant:
To add parameters to a curl command, you can include them in the URL or as part of the command itself using the `-d` or `--data` flag. Here are some examples:

1. Including parameters in the URL:


```sql
curl -X GET 'https://api.example.com/users?name=John&age=30' -H 'Authorization: Bearer your\_token\_here'
```
In this example, we are making a GET request to the API endpoint at `https://api.example.com/users`, with the `name` and `age` parameters set to `John` and `30`, respectively. Note that the parameters are included in the URL after the `?` character, and separated by the `&` character.

1. Including parameters in the request body using the `-d` or `--data` flag:


```python
curl -X POST 'https://api.example.com/users' -H 'Authorization: Bearer your\_token\_here' -d 'name=John&age=30'
```
In this example, we are making a POST request to the API endpoint at `https://api.example.com/users`, and sending the `name` and `age` parameters in the request body using the `-d` or `--data` flag. Note that the parameters are included as a string of key-value pairs, separated by the `&` character.

1. Including parameters in a JSON payload using the `-d` or `--data` flag:


```css
curl -X POST 'https://api.example.com/users' -H 'Authorization: Bearer your_token_here' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"John", "age":30}'
```
In this example, we are making a POST request to the API endpoint at `https://api.example.com/users`, and sending the `name` and `age` parameters in a JSON payload using the `-d` or `--data` flag. Note that we are also setting the `Content-Type` header to `application/json` to indicate that we are sending JSON data.
